notes: The invocation the Python test uses, with --resolution at its default of 1000 and a positive upstream value that the tool negates in place. 401 rows plus two header lines.

--resolution/-r was never exercised by the Python suite. It is both the step and part of the stop value, since the loop runs to range[1] + resolution exclusive, so the downstream end is included: five rows from -20000 to 20000.
The upstream value given negative, which is the spelling the help text documents and which skips the negation branch. 201 rows.
The threshold is parsed as a float and written with str(), so -tv 1 prints as 1.0 and not as 1. A single row, at zero.

repr() of a small float switches to exponent notation at 1e-05 and spells it without a trailing zero in the mantissa, which printf's %g does not do. The case exists to pin hicx::npy::float_repr against CPython on this tool's only piece of formatting.
